question: Will Jannik Sinner win the 2026 Men's US Open?
rationale:

Source: Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/8/9/jannik-sinner-withdraws-from-cincinnati-open-with-knee-injury). His quote: "My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept that I'm not ready to compete yet." This means Sinner will enter the US Open (starts August 23) with ZERO warm-up competitive matches on hard courts since Wimbledon (July). Missing both Montreal and Cincinnati means the injury is significant enough that the medical team is not willing to risk an aggravation in a warm-up — that signals a non-trivial injury.

Injury-adjusted p_hat: 0.42. The market at 0.525 applies a "regime persistence" discount for the injury but still prices him as a 52.5% favorite despite zero recent match play. This overestimates his chances by approximately 10 percentage points.

Carlos Alcaraz (2-time Wimbledon champion) is at only 13.5% — the market sees a huge gap between Sinner and the field, which reflects his dominance when healthy, but less accurately reflects injury-compromised Sinner vs the full field.

Net edge on NO: p_hat NO = 0.58 vs market NO implied = 0.47. Net edge ~9% after spread. Medium conviction (sports markets are generally efficient, but injury information is a specific knowable new fact).

Bet is independent of all open positions (Bet 7: US-Iran, Bet 10: Apple).

question: Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by August 31?
rationale:
Betting YES on Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by August 31, 2026. Resolution criterion: "a diplomatic agreement between Oman and Iran... an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between Oman and Iran" over Hormuz traffic.

Current status (as of August 10):
- August 5: Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-05/iran-says-agreement-on-hormuz-shipping-route-reached-with-oman), Fortune (https://fortune.com/2026/08/07/iran-agreement-oman-strait-of-hormuz-shipping/), Al Jazeera: Iran and Oman "reached agreement on proposed Hormuz shipping routes."
- August 8: Iranian FM spokesman Baghaei (CNN, https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/08/world/live-news/iran-war-trump): joint statement is "under review and in the final drafting stage."
- The agreed terms include: geographical coordinates for shipping corridor, joint coordination center, inbound/outbound lane separation, vessel monitoring, Iran-administered maritime security.

The Polymarket criterion requires ONLY an Iran-Oman bilateral agreement — not US approval, not full Hormuz reopening. Iran explicitly stated the agreement "does not mean the full reopening of the Strait" (citing need for additional US concessions for that), but a bilateral Iran-Oman agreement for a partial managed shipping corridor appears to already be substantively agreed. The remaining step is formal publication of the joint statement, which is in "final drafting stage" as of August 8.

21 days remain until August 31. With the draft ready and both sides having agreed on the core terms (coordinates, corridor structure, joint center), the probability the formal statement is published by August 31 is high. Main risk: Iran-US negotiation breakdown derails the deal, OR Iran decides to withhold the agreement as leverage in broader US-Iran talks. NPR (https://www.npr.org/2026/08/07/nx-s1-5923962/iran-says-agreement-with-oman-for-strait-of-hormuz-prohibits-u-s-and-israeli-vessels) confirms Iran's statement explicitly bans US and Israeli vessels, suggesting Iran is comfortable with bilateral Oman deal independent of US approval.

p_hat YES = 0.78. Market ask = 0.66. Net edge ~10%.

CONCENTRATION NOTE: This is the 2nd Iran-correlated open bet (Bet 7 = US-Iran MOU extension NO). These are correlated with the broader Iran geopolitical situation but are DIFFERENT real-world outcomes (different parties, different agreements) and are largely anti-correlated in terms of directional risk: a formal US-Iran MOU extension (which would hurt Bet 7 NO) is SEPARATE from an Iran-Oman bilateral agreement (which would help this bet). The two bets are within the maximum 2-Iran-bet concentration limit.
